description: Use when the user asks to rebuild, clone, copy, port, restyle or 'make it look like' part of a real website, or wants a site's section as Tailwind, HTML+CSS, React (JSX) or Vue - or as a file to import into a site builder: framework=elementor for an Elementor template (WordPress), framework=shopify for a Shopify theme section. Give it the URL and, when the user named a part of the page, section (hero, header, footer, pricing, features, testimonials, faq, cta) - never invent a CSS selector. With neither, it auto-detects the hero; every call also returns `sections`, each other extractable section with a label and a ready selector for a follow-up call. Returns a self-contained component with the page's real resolved styles (true colors, fonts, spacing, copy) plus the tokens and assets it uses, so you adapt real values instead of estimating from a screenshot. For jsx/vue, repeated structures collapse into a data array rendered with .map()/v-for; ::before/::after come back as real elements; @keyframes ship in the css field. The `theme` field says which theme the code actually is - sites with a prefers-color-scheme dark variant return the light branch unless you pass theme='dark'; say which you returned. Not for: whole-page scraping, page text, or sites that need a login. Loads the page in a real browser and reads the styles, theme and images it actually shows, on every plan at no extra cost - no need to pass render=true. Large inline SVGs (logo walls, illustrations) come back as hosted files so the code stays small enough to use as-is (inline_svg=true keeps them inline). Hand `code` to the user unchanged instead of rewriting it, and give them `previewUrl`, which shows the returned code rendered as a page with a Download HTML button. When rebuilding a whole page, extract each section and give them `pagePreviewUrl`: every section extracted so far, assembled in page order, also downloadable.

framework.description: The code to generate (default tailwind). 'elementor' returns an importable Elementor template: tell the user to save `code` as a .json file and import it in WordPress under Templates > Saved Templates > Import. 'shopify' returns a theme section: save `code` as sections/<name>.liquid in the theme, then add it from the theme editor. Use the theme code editor's sections folder, not a Custom Liquid block (that block is capped at 50 KB and cannot hold the schema). Both arrive as one styled HTML block (edited as code, not as native widgets), with the section's responsive and hover styles included and its CSS scoped so it cannot clash with the theme. Give the user the file contents complete and unmodified.

fresh.description: Skip the 24-hour cache and re-extract the live page - use when the site just changed and a cached result would be stale. Charged normally; the fresh result replaces the cached copy.

inline_svg.description: Keep large inline SVGs (logos, illustrations) inline in `code` instead of hosted files. Only when the user needs fully self-contained code: a logo wall can add 50+ KB.

name.description: Component name for the jsx target (default ExtractedSection). Ignored by tailwind, html and vue. Renaming never re-runs the extraction - it costs 0 credits on a cached section.

render.description: Force a real browser so the page's JavaScript runs before it is read. Slower, and adds 5 credits. Usually not needed: when the plain read comes back as a JavaScript app shell or the site refuses it (401/403/406) or timed out, the server already re-runs the page in a browser by itself at no extra cost, and usage.autoRender says so. Pass it for images, videos or Lottie that only load on scroll, with screenshot=true, or when a result is still thin after that automatic pass. If a 403 says the browser was refused too, the site cannot be extracted - do not retry. extract_code always runs in a real browser at no extra cost, so render=true is not needed there (only together with screenshot=true). On extract_design_tokens, render=true only permits the browser: the plain read still runs first, and the 5 credits are charged only if the browser was actually needed.

screenshot.description: Requires render=true. Adds a screenshot field to the result: a public URL of a capture of the page (live 7 days), taken by the same browser that rendered it. Pass true for the 1440x900 viewport or 'full' for the entire page height. No extra credits beyond the render surcharge. Useful for showing the user what the extracted site looks like.

section.description: Which part of the page, by name - use this when the user asked for the pricing, footer, header/nav, features, testimonials, FAQ or call-to-action block. Resolved on the page itself from its ids, classes, headings and, failing those, its content (prices, blockquotes, FAQ items), so it works without seeing the markup and on pages that label nothing. Omit for the hero. If the page has no such section you get the hero plus a `note` listing what is there.

selector.description: CSS selector for the section, ONLY when you have one from a previous result's `sections` list (e.g. "section.pricing-grid"). Do not guess selectors: a selector that matches nothing falls back to the hero with a `note`, and the guess costs a call. Prefer `section` for named parts of a page.

theme.description: Which colour scheme to extract (default light). Pass 'dark' when the user is looking at the site in dark mode or asks for the dark version: the page's prefers-color-scheme: dark rules and custom properties become the component itself instead of riding along as dark: variants. Works whether the site expresses its themes as @media (prefers-color-scheme) or as a root attribute/class the CSS is scoped to ([data-theme=dark], html.dark). Sites that switch themes purely in JavaScript cannot be selected this way - you get the page default plus a hint saying so. No extra credits.

name: extract_code

autoDetected.description: True when the hero was auto-detected rather than passed in

code.description: The generated, paste-ready component code. For jsx/vue, repeated structures (tiers, cards, list items) are collapsed into a data array rendered with .map()/v-for. For elementor this is the complete template JSON (a .json file); for shopify the complete section file (a .liquid file) - hand either over whole

css.description: Companion CSS: always set for framework=html; for tailwind/jsx/vue it carries the @keyframes the section uses (add to the global stylesheet); null for elementor/shopify, whose file already contains its CSS

framework.description: tailwind | html | jsx | vue | elementor | shopify

hint.description: Only present when the extraction looks degraded (client-rendered page, runtime-injected styles) - says what to do (the server has already tried a browser where one would help); on a render=true call the styles could not be resolved even in a browser, do not retry

note.description: Present when the requested selector or section was not found and the hero was returned instead - says what was asked for and which sections the page does have. Tell the user.

pagePreviewUrl.description: The whole page: every section of this URL extracted in the last day, assembled in page order, with a Download HTML button. Grows as more sections are extracted - give it to the user after a whole-page rebuild

previewUrl.description: A page showing this section rendered from the same extraction (as HTML + CSS), so it looks exactly like the code you got. Give it to the user so they can compare it with the live site

section.description: The named section that was resolved, when one was requested

sections.description: Every extractable section on the page - call again with one of these selectors for a specific part

order.description: Where the section starts on the page among the listed ones, 1 = topmost - sort by it to rebuild a whole page in sequence

selector.description: The CSS selector that was extracted

summary.description: What was extracted, at a glance. styledCoverage (0-100) is the quality signal: the % of elements the cascade found styles for

svgNote.description: Present when large inline SVGs were moved to hosted files - how many and how much smaller the code got

theme.description: light | dark: which one the code you just received actually is. Measured from the page, never echoed from your request - so if you asked for a theme the site cannot serve, this reports what you really got. Tell the user which theme they got when it may not match what they see on the site

tokens.description: Design tokens the extracted section actually uses

truncation_note.description: Present when the result was trimmed - says what was dropped and how to get more.

usage.description: Credit usage for the authed key (spent, remaining, monthly limit).

title: Extract section as code
